name: IA-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+15 district lean keeps the seat firmly Republican even with the incumbent off the ballot
McGowan's fundraising edge: $863k raised and $444k on hand versus $42k for Dawson
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 3%
No public polling; a Dem-favorable national environment is the main offset
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean and McGowan's clear money advantage outweigh a favorable national environment for Democrats, and prediction markets align with a comfortable Republican margin in this open-seat race.
model.watch: Fresh polling or significant Democratic outside spending showing a single-digit race would justify moving this toward Lean R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Randy Feenstra (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Iowa's fourth district carries a partisan lean of roughly fifteen points toward Republicans, and Randy Feenstra's retirement to run for governor leaves the seat open without changing its fundamental color. Fundraising reports show Republican Chris McGowan with a decisive financial edge: about $863,000 raised and $444,000 on hand, plus roughly $173,000 in outside support, against about $259,000 raised and $42,000 on hand for Democrat David Dawson. No outside money has been spent against McGowan.

Prediction markets give Dawson roughly a three percent chance, and no public polls of the general election exist. A national environment that has favored Democrats trims the Republican advantage, but not enough to put the district in play. With the seat open and no polling to refine the picture, the race remains likely, though not certain, to stay in Republican hands.
